top_news.title: Japan Inflation Rises Above BOJ Target Level, Backing Rate Hikes
top_news.summary: Japan’s key price gauge rose above the Bank of Japan’s target level for the first time this year, supporting the case for a widely expected BOJ interest rate hike in December.

top_news.title: Australia’s Victoria State Approves $700 Million Gas Project
top_news.summary: Australia’s Victoria state has approved the production license for a A$1 billion ($700 million) natural gas project to help avoid a forecast gas shortage.

top_news.title: Treasuries Surge as Worldwide Worries Spark Rush to Safety
top_news.summary: Treasuries rallied for their best day in more than two years, surging across the board as a deepening rout in AI-related shares, market turmoil in France and fresh Mideast tensions all combined to make US government debt the investment of choice for anxious traders.

top_news.title: Australian Growth Likely Slower Than Expected, Chalmers Says
top_news.summary: Australia’s growth will likely be slower than the 1.75% forecast in May’s budget, Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Friday, as a series of rate hikes and rising inflation start to bite on the economy.

top_news.title: What a 35-Hour Train Ride Reveals About Vietnam’s Future
top_news.summary: Vietnam is betting big on a $65 billion high-speed railway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Construction is set to start in late 2027 and take at least a decade to complete. The line could cut the roughly 35-hour journey to just six hours. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: New York City Bans Horse-Drawn Carriages After Decade-Long Battle
top_news.summary: New York’s City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending a Central Park tourist staple dating to the 19th century after years of debate over the horses’ place on city streets. Bloomberg's  Laura Nahmias explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Typhoon Champi Shuts Taiwan’s $5 Trillion Stock Market
top_news.summary: Taiwan’s stock exchange will shut Friday as Typhoon Champi approaches the island, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds that prompted authorities to shut offices and schools in the capital city of Taipei.

top_news.title: BlackRock's Senra on Investment Shifts, Wealth Transfer
top_news.summary: Armando Senra, Head of the Americas Institutional Business at BlackRock, said family offices generally view geopolitical tensions as a source of short-term market and allocation effects, rather than a reason for major long-term portfolio changes. He said investors are attentive to current events but are maintaining broader trends seen among institutional clients: expanding private-market exposure with greater diversification and using ETFs for both active and index strategies. top_news.title: Mickey Drexler on Decker Results and Retail Outlook
top_news.summary: Mickey Drexler, Chair of Alex Mill and Former CEO and chair of J. Crew, tells Bloomberg that apparel retailers need to do more to give consumers a reason to buy. He says product, discounting and especially newness matter, while arguing that fashion has put too little emphasis on creativity and reinvention. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Kroger CFO: We Are an Agent for the Consumer
top_news.summary: Kroger CFO David Kennerley discusses the company plans to invest $5 billion in consumer value, including affordable groceries and simpler promotions, while seeking to fund the effort through $4 billion in structural cost savings. Kennerley said the company is seeing a slight uptick in inflation but remains within the range it projected earlier in the year, and will accept supplier price increases only when justified. He speaks with Romaine Bostick in "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
